en: The Sūtra of the Great White Parasol Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Great Master of Wondrous Eloquence from Central India, Jñānagarbha,
and the chief translator, the Monk Chen-ji (Jñānajñāna), and others.
Homage to the most excellent and supreme Guru. Now,
for one who wishes to practice the White Parasol Goddess (Śvetāśvāsottarā), in a quiet room:
Having sat upon a soft, steady woolen rug,
one should then make this aspiration:
"For the sake of all sentient beings of the six realms."
Having made the aspiration, "May I attain ultimate,
perfect enlightenment so that all beings may be liberated from saṃsāra," he resolved.
Visualize the assembly of the Buddha Sitātapatrā in the space before you.
Having recited the three refuges with a mind of sincere devotion,
the assembly of the Buddha melts into light.
Absorb it into yourself, and as you become light,
recite the *svamā* mantra while contemplating that all things are empty.
In the space above that, upon a lotus and moon disc,
visualize a white syllable Oṃ. From the syllable Oṃ,
light rays radiate forth.
The light returns once more;
the seed-syllables transform into a white parasol with a golden handle,
the top of which is adorned with the syllable Oṃ.
The syllables emit light and return;
the seed-syllables transform into the White Parasol Mother (Sitatapatrā),
who has one face, two arms, and three eyes.
Seated in the vajra-paryaṅka posture,
his right hand forms the mudrā of fearlessness,
and his left hand holds a white parasol at his chest.
Adorned with various kinds of necklaces,
his body was as pure white as a snow mountain illuminated by the light of the sun,
manifesting the mark of joy while revealing the absence of intrinsic nature.
One should contemplate it as being like a reflection in a mirror.
When wishing to recite the mantra,
[one should visualize it] upon a solar disc atop a lotus flower within one's own heart.
The syllable Oṃ encircles the heart; there,
the mantra and the long and short dhāraṇīs emit light,
dispelling all karmic obstacles and hindrances of oneself and others.
Once you have cleared away thoughts of interruption and the like, you may then recite.
If you become weary and wish to offer food as an act of merit, place the food before you.
Recite the three-syllable mantra Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ to consecrate it,
transforming it into nectar.
In the space before you, invoke the goddess Sitātapatrā as the foremost of the assembly.
Having [visualized] the Mother of Darkness dwelling upon the twenty-two mountain tombs,
as well as the seven kinds of Buddhas and the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the ten directions,
surrounded by the three types of those endowed with excellence, the Pure Brahmā, and Śakra; and so forth.
Visualize that the tongue transforms into a vajra-light tube.
Recite the mantra for offering food as follows:
Oṃ sarvata-thāgata-uṣṇīṣa-śīrṣa-dharmadhātu-hūṃ phaṭ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ maḥ kṣe kṣe kṣe kṣi kṣi. Having recited this three or five times, [proceed].
Then, having completed the recitations, praises, prayers,
and petitions for one's aspirations, one should perform the ritual of escorting the Buddha’s assembly back.
Having cast the food for alms in a clean place, dedicate the roots of virtue.

Oṃ ārya-tathāgatodbhava-śrī-vajra-dhara-mahā-kalpānta-jvalana-teja-rāśi-vanditāya namaḥ. (Sanskrit: Homage to the Noble Mother Sitātapatrā, the White Parasol, who emerged from the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, the Invincible Dhāraṇī; salutation to the Supreme Triple Gem. In the Chinese language: *Jingli zuishang sanbao* (Homage to the Supreme Triple Gem).
Thus have I heard. At one time,
the Blessed One was dwelling in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, in the excellent and sublime abode of the devas known as Sudharmā.
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the host of Śakra, Lord of Devas,
the Bhagavān sat upon a lotus throne and entered the samādhi known as the Universal Observation of the Uṣṇīṣa.
Then, the Bhagavān swiftly brought forth from the crown of his head this dhāraṇī mantra and the practice of its dharma.
Homage to the Buddha and to all the bodhisattvas!
Homage to the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Sublime Dharma.
Homage to the Saṅgha.
Homage to the seven koṭis of truly ultimate, perfectly awakened ones, together with the assembly of śrāvakas.
Homage to all those who have destroyed the enemies of the world.
Homage to all those who have entered the stream and so forth.
Homage to all those who have attained the stage of once-returning.
Homage to all those who have attained the stage of non-returning.
Homage to all those in the world who have truly transcended [the mundane].
Homage to all those who have entered into reality.
Homage to the celestial sages, whether they cast curses or possess the power to bestow blessings.
Homage to all those who have attained accomplishment through the recitation and retention of vidyā-mantras.
Homage to the Pure Brahmā.
Homage to Śakra. Homage to the lords of asceticism, such as Kṛśāśva, who possess beauty and the power to cause others to withdraw from their austerities.
Homage to the one endowed with excellence, who is honored by the Five-Fingered Seal (Pañcamudrā) and is the refuge of the Unattached Son (Vajrapāṇi).
Homage to the one endowed with excellence, who can destroy the three-tiered palace city, dwells amidst the charnel grounds, and is the refuge of all the Mātṛkās.
Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata of the Buddha-lineage.
Homage to the Buddha of the Lotus-lineage.
Homage to the Buddha of the Vajra-lineage.
Homage to the Buddha of the Jewel-Gem Lineage.
Homage to the Buddha of the Great Elephant Lineage.
Homage to the Buddha of the Youthful Child Lineage.
Homage to the Buddha Nāgottama.
Homage to the Buddha Śūraṃgamasamudgataśastrarāja.
Homage to the Buddha Amitābha.
Homage to Akṣobhya Buddha.
Homage to Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharāja Buddha.
Homage to Śālarājapuṣpaphalasamṛddha Buddha.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Ratnottama-rāja Buddha.
Homage to Samantabhadra-sarvottama Buddha.
I pay homage to the Buddha, Lord of All Vidyās.
I pay homage to the Buddha, King of Fragrant Incense with Perfect Eyes.
Having paid homage to them, [I proceed].
The Bhagavatī Mother, the White Parasol Goddess who emerges from the uṣṇīṣas of all Tathāgatas, the peerless Great Repeller;
by her, all emerging malevolent spirits and māras are decisively subdued.
It can also decisively overcome all other vidyā-mantras;
it can also avert untimely and accidental deaths;
and it can cause sentient beings to be liberated from all fetters.
It can also avert and ward off all hatred, resentment, and evil dreams;
it can also destroy the eighty-four thousand malevolent spirits;
and it can bring joy to the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
It can also subdue the eight great lunar mansions;
it can also avert and ward off all enemies and仇讎 (enemies);
and it can also destroy all extremely violent, evil, hateful, and malevolent dreams.
She is also able to rescue and deliver from the perils of poison, weapons, water, fire, and the like.
There is none who can oppose her: the Great Kṣetrapālī, the Great Dāṇḍapāṇī, the Great Balavatī, the Great Jvalantī, the Great Tejovatī, the Great Sitātapatrā, and the Great Balavatī.
Blazing Garlanded White-Robed Mother, Noble Tārā with Frowning Wrath, Victorious Power,
Vajra-named Rosary; Lotus Radiance, Vajra-named Invincible,
Rosary-holder, Vajra-Wall and others, the Destroyer Mother.
The Mother who is honored by the Buddhas such as Maitreya; the Great Mother endowed with gentle marks and majestic power, the Noble Tārā and the One of Great Might;
the Invincible Vajra-Iron-Chain Mother and the Vajra Youth who holds the seed-syllable; the Vajrapāṇi-seed and the Rosary-holder.
The Great Crimson One and Ratnolkā; the Seed-Syllable Vidyā and Vajraśekhara;
the One of Profound Form and Vajrī; the Golden-Colored Light and Locanā;
Vajrapradīpā and Pāṇḍaravāsini; Padmanetrā and Candraprabhā.
Because all those powers are gathered within this mudrā, may it protect me,
may it protect me! Oṃ ṛṣidattā-prajñe tathāgatoṣṇīṣa...

NAḌAKĀRA HŪṂ KROṄ CAKĀRA ŚRĪTE NAṄ GYIRA HASA HASI RĀMI ṆAṄ SA NAḌAKĀRA HŪṂ KROṄ ĀŚRID ṆAṄ ZHEDE ṆAṄ NA SE HASA UḌID DRA NA MA PU RA SATTA NA.
Gara hūṃ phreṃ ahi dadna mama kṣetra-hrada-nemike nemine neme saṇe gara hūṃ phreṃ rasekara ṭhaḥ. May the Bhagavatī Mother,
the White Parasol emerged from the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, protect me!
She is indeed the Mother of Buddhas, the Great Vajra-Cūḍā-Paritrāṇī,
the Mother endowed with a thousand great arms.
There is the Great Thousand-Headed Mother,
who possesses one million koṭis of eyes, the non-dual, blazing, and fully endowed with all marks, the Vajra Broad and White Mother,
the Sovereign of the mandala within the three realms.
At all times, protect me! Protect me! Oṃ!

From the perils of kings, the perils of thieves, the perils of fire, the perils of water, the perils of poisons, the perils of weapons, the perils of foreign armies, the perils of famine, the perils of enemies, the perils of epidemics, the perils of lightning, the perils of untimely and accidental death, the perils of earthquakes, the perils of shooting stars, the perils of royal punishment, the perils of devas, the perils of nāgas, the perils of lightning strikes, the perils of those who fly through the air, and the perils of wrathful wild beasts.

Furthermore, among all the celestial māras, nāga-māras, non-celestial māras, wind-māras, spirit-māras, sky-faring māras, gandharva-māras, doubt-māras, large-bellied māras, obstructing-māras, yakṣa-māras, preta-māras, ḍākinī-māras, flesh-eating māras, emerging māras, flask-and-bag māras, stench-māras, body-odor-māras, those who cause emaciation, those who cause forgetfulness, those who cause madness, those who cause nightmares, those who cause suppression, and the Aśvinī-māras—among all these, may I attain peace, security, and auspiciousness.

Furthermore, among those such as the spirits who seize power, the spirits who seize countenance, the spirits who consume the birth-chamber, the blood-drinking spirits, the spirits who consume the womb, the flesh-eating spirits, the fat-eating spirits, the marrow-eating spirits, the spirits who wear fat as clothing, the life-taking spirits, the spirits who consume vomit, the spirits who consume excrement, the spirits who consume urine, the spirits who consume secretions from the orifices, the spirits who consume remnants, the spirits who consume saliva, the spirits who consume nasal mucus, the spirits who consume spittle, the spirits who consume pus, the spirits who consume offered food, the spirits who consume garlands, the spirits who consume fragrances, the spirits who consume incense, the spirit who seizes the mind, the flower-eating spirits, the fruit-eating spirits, the sprout-eating spirits, and the spirits who consume burnt offerings.
May I obtain peace, security, and auspiciousness.

All those [obstacles] and all the vidyā-mantras created by Māras—by this I sever them and strike them with the vajra. All the vidyā-mantras created by Vyāghrapada—by this I sever them and strike them with the vajra.
The vidyā-mantras created by the ḍākas and ḍākinīs are severed by this; one shall strike them with the vajra.
The vidyā-mantras created by the Great Lord of Beasts are severed by this; one shall strike them with the vajra.
With this [mantra], sever the vidyā-mantras created by the Son of No-Love (Anurāga-putra) and strike them with the mallet.
With this [mantra], sever the vidyā-mantras created by the Sky-Flyer (Khecarī), the Realizer (Tattvākārin), and others, and strike them with the mallet.
The vidyā-mantras created by Mahākāla, the Mātṛkās, and others—decide them with these and strike them with the vajra.
The vidyā-mantras created by those who carry human head-bowls—decide them with these and strike them with the vajra.
With the *vidyā-mantra* composed by Liṅgava and Makṣikākārī, which was perfected in the past, one shall resolve this and strike it with the mallet.
With the *vidyā-mantra* composed by the four sisters, one shall resolve this and strike it with the mallet.
One shall sever with this mantra and strike with the vajra those mantras composed by Bīṣma, Upendra, Kṛtānta, Prajāpati, and the like;
one shall sever with this mantra and strike with the vajra those mantras composed by those who are not virtuous or pure.
One who has destroyed the spells created by enemies shall sever them with this and strike them with the vajra.
One who has transcended desire shall sever the spells created [by others] with this and strike them with the vajra.
With this vidyā-mantra composed by the Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, one shall sever [the enemy] and strike them with the vajra.
Homage to the Bhagavatī Mother, the White Parasol Goddess who emerged from the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.
Protect me! Protect me! Oṃ akṣitāra kṣikopa ramasi budhyata ṅaḥ saṃkṣipta marda rīḍa rīḍa kṣe kṣe khara khara mikhara mikha.

Hre phaṭ sarvam asramaye hre phaṭ sarvaṃ kṣudrān ḍākinī hre phaṭ caṇḍagrahamaṇḍale hre phaṭ sarvam ālarkadaṃśaka hre phaṭ mṛtyuṃ caṭaye hre phaṭ.
Cāṭa-mṛte jihvāgra-śeṣe gṛdhe hūṃ phaṭ | sarvam-aka-u-māriṇi hūṃ phaṭ | khaṭvāṅge hūṃ phaṭ | māheśvara-tāluka-gṛdhe hūṃ phaṭ | mahā-vajra-śikhara-kale akāre ||

Oṃ śrī-vajra-jvālā-mālini hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-śikhare hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-krodha-hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-garjite hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-narte hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-bhīme hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-saṃhare hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-raudre hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-karāle hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ śrī-vajra-yamāntake hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vighnāntakṛt oṃ vajra-āditya-mahāteja-samaya-dharma-teja oṃ vighna.
May all sentient beings who harbor feelings of hatred, aversion, or the like toward me [be pacified].
Regarding those who give rise to violent and evil thoughts and so forth,
they are able to seize one's majestic power and the like;
furthermore, there are the *āśrayaharaṇa* spirits (those who steal the physical countenance).
The spirits who consume food and produce,
the spirits who consume blood,
and the spirits who consume congealed fat.
The flesh-eating ghosts,
the fat-eating ghosts,
and the marrow-eating ghosts.
The *garbha-vastra-bhakṣa* spirits,
the *jīvita-hara* spirits,
the *vānta-bhakṣa* spirits, and so forth.
The ghosts who eat excrement,
the ghosts who eat urine, and the ghosts who eat the secretions from the bodily orifices.
The ghosts who eat leftovers,
the ghosts who eat saliva,
and the ghosts who eat nasal mucus.
The saliva-eating spirits,
the pus-eating spirits,
and the food-offering-eating spirits.
The *bhojana-mālā* spirits,
the *gandha-bhojana* spirits,
and the *gandha* spirits.
The flower-eating spirits,
the fruit-eating spirits,
and the sprout-eating spirits.
Those who consume the offerings of burnt sacrifices,
those whose minds are possessed by transgressions and faults,
and those whose minds are possessed by feelings of aversion and suspicion.
Those who possess violent and evil minds,
as well as all the celestial māras,
the nāga-māras, and so forth.
Neither the celestial Māras,
nor the wind-demon Māras,
nor the space-flying Māras.
The Gandharva Māras and so forth;
the Kinnara Māras and so forth;
the Mahodara Māras and so forth.
The obstructing māras,
the yakṣa māras, the preta māras, and so forth.
The flesh-eating māras,
the emerging māras, the jar-and-bag māras, and so forth.
The Foul-smelling Māras and so forth;
the Body-odorous Māras and so forth;
those who cause emaciation, the Withering Māras and so forth.
It causes the mad demons and so forth;
it causes the enchanting demons and so forth;
it causes the forgetful demons and so forth.
Subjugating the māras and so forth;
the ḍākinīs, māras, and so forth; the nakṣatra of Revatī, the māras, and so forth.
The Mara of the Lord of Hell and his retinue;
the Mara of the Mother of the Skandhas and his retinue;
and the Mara of Wandering Everywhere Adorned with Garlands and his retinue.
Balamā and others;
furthermore, there shall be pestilence for one day,
as well as all illnesses lasting two days, three days, four days, or seven days.
Constant epidemics, inexhaustible epidemics,
and the emergence of diseases characterized by piercing pain arise based on wind.
Diseases arise based on bile;
diseases arise based on phlegm;
diseases arise based on the combination of both.
May all diseases, including physical ailments and the like, be dispelled.

Furthermore, may illnesses of the body parts—such as loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, neck disease, heart disease, throat disease, ear disease, tooth disease, feverish affliction of the mind, brain disease, pain in the ribs, pain in the vertebrae, abdominal disease, waist disease, anal disease, thigh disease, calf disease, hand disease, foot disease, and diseases of the limbs and various extremities—all be eliminated.
I pray that you may dispel [all obstacles] and grant protection.
O Great White Parasol Goddess, Vajroṣṇīṣa Mahāparitrāṇī:
by this, may those who emerge within twelve yojanas—whether they be vetālas or ḍākinīs—[be subdued].
Furthermore, there are pestilential diseases, scabies, itchy sores, smallpox, leprosy, cracked and fissured sores, hemorrhoids, burns, abscesses, and malignant sores.
Additionally, there are emaciating and terrifying illnesses, as well as poisons from jewels, compounded poisons, and poisons from malevolent incantations, along with the calamities of fire and water.
Furthermore, there are quarrels, feuds, injuries, untimely deaths, and premature mortality.

Moreover, there are the *ḍrīmābhuja* insects, the *ḍrīrat* insects, vipers, scorpions, venomous snakes, weasels, lions, tigers, bears, brown bears, and water-beasts, as well as gadflies and flies that take the lives of others.
All those vidyā-mantras shall completely bind all modes of conduct and bind all other vidyā-mantras.
This is the vidyā-mantra that binds all Māras; may it bind them all.

Having written this *Sitātapatrā Aparājitā Mahāpratisarā*, which emerges from the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas,
upon birch bark, white cotton cloth, or tree bark;
Whether worn upon the body or around the neck,
one will remain so until the end of one's life;
neither poison nor weapons shall be able to cause harm.
Fire cannot burn it; water cannot sweep it away.
Precious poisons cannot affect it, nor can compounded poisons harm it.
Incantations and poisons cannot destroy it, and untimely death cannot invade it.
All enemies, māras, and all evil associates, as well as in every place,
shall be delighted by, loved by, and respected by him. Furthermore,
he will be honored by the eighty-four thousand *koṭis* of vajra-lineages, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
They shall also provide protection, rescue, and shelter;
they will act with pleasing intent and be held in love and respect.
Furthermore, for eighty-four thousand great eons, they will attain the knowledge of past lives.
Furthermore, in every lifetime and place of birth, they do not receive bodies such as those of obstructive rākṣasas, hungry ghosts, or those with foul odors or bodily stench;
nor do they receive the body of a poor person among humans.
Furthermore, they are endowed with the merit and fortune of immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Bhagavāns, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Moreover, they constantly maintain the Great Repeller, the White Parasol Mother, which emerges from the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas and is invincible by any other.
Thus, even one who does not practice the holy life accomplishes the holy life;
one who cannot endure accomplishes endurance;
and that which is impure becomes pure.
One who lacks the *upavāsa* precepts obtains the *upavāsa* precepts;
one who does not observe the fast becomes one who has observed the fast.
Even if one has committed the five sins of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*), they can be purified without remainder.
All karmic obstacles from the past will be completely extinguished.
If a woman desires a son,
she should uphold this Great Repelling Mother, the White Parasol Goddess emerging from the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, who is invincible by any other.
One will obtain a son endowed with a full lifespan, merit, and power;
after the end of his life, he will be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
Furthermore, there shall be no human diseases, cattle diseases, livestock diseases, or epidemics.
Furthermore, in cases of injury, the onset of disease, obstacles,
or amidst all other military forces engaged in battle,
one may employ this Great Repelling Mother, the White Parasol Goddess emerging from the uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, who is invincible by any other.
Having placed it upon the top of a banner and performed extensive offerings,
one should then set the banner atop the gate of a great city,
or within a palace, or within a village.
Whether in a village, in a valley or plain, or in a place of solitude,
one should perform a vast offering at the site of the Great Averting Mother, who is invincible to all others.
Then one will be able to swiftly bring about peace within the realm;
furthermore, one will be able to soften and subdue pestilence, obstacles,
harm, strife, and all other foreign military forces.
The *Mārā-bhañji-māra-paritrāṇa-mantra* for the expulsion of Māras and protection:

The Perfectly Awakened One and the Bodhisattvas,
along with the gods, asuras, and humans,
together with the gandharvas and all the world.
All were filled with great joy and, in the presence of the place where the Bhagavān had spoken, they offered this praise:
Oṃ! Upon a sublime lotus moon-disc seat, you sit in the vajra-paryaṅka posture, your body white in color.
With your left hand at your heart, you hold a white parasol; to the one endowed with the white umbrella, we offer praise and homage.
With her right hand she forms the mudrā of fearlessness; with a joyful smile, her body possesses graceful elegance.
Embraced by all the Perfectly Awakened Ones, O Mother of Buddhas, I prostrate to you who are praised in all places.
You dwell where all sentient beings are subdued, manifesting various bodies according to their kind.
I pay homage and praise the Mother who dwells in the most exquisite and delightful Array of Great Jewels.

Oṃ! You are the invincible Great Yakṣī, the Great Club-wielding Mother, the Mother of Great Power, the Great Blazing Mother, the Mother of Great Majesty, the Mother of the Great White Parasol, and the Mother of Great Strength.
Blazing Garlanded White-Robed Mother, Noble Tārā with Greatly Frowning Wrath,
Known as the Holy Vajra of the World, Lotus Radiance, Vajra-named,
Invincible One who possesses the rosary, And Mother who destroys the Vajra Wall and all else.
The Mother who is worshipped by the Buddhas such as Maitreya; the Great Mother endowed with gentle marks and majestic power;
the Noble Tārā, the Mother of Great Might; the Invincible Vajra-Chain Mother;
the Vajra Youthful One who holds the seed-syllable; the Vajrapāṇi-seed, the Holder of the Rosary.
The Great Red One and Ratnolkā; the Seed-Syllable Vidyā and Vajraśikhī;
the One with Profound Features and Vajranetrī; the Golden-Colored Radiance and Cakṣuṣmatī;
the Vajrapradīpā and Śvetā; Padmanetrī and Candrāvatī.
Homage and praise to the assembly of mudrās; To the Bhagavatī Sitātapatrā, the one who emerged from the uṣṇīṣa of Śākyamuni;
To the Vajroṣṇīṣavijayā, the thousand-armed and thousand-eyed Mahāmāyūrī; To the Great Koṭīlocanā.
Non-dual, blazing, and endowed with all characteristics, Vajra, Vast and Great White Mother, Sovereign of the Center of the Three Worlds— O Supreme One, grant me protection! Oṃ!
From kings, thieves, fear, water, fire, poison, weapons, famine, malevolent spirits, and disease.
May thunderbolts, untimely death, and premature demise; earthquakes, royal punishments, and the like;
lightning striking from the sky and all such terrors; and the great calamities of wild beasts, tigers, and the rest—be dispelled at all times.
Grant me protection in every moment against these and the various obstructing māras of the celestial realm.
May you grant protection at all times against those who seize one's power, as well as hungry ghosts, and among the great diseases such as wind,
bile, and phlegm; and from the afflictions of greed, ignorance, and hatred, the ten non-virtuous actions,
the five deeds of immediate retribution, and all obstructing natural misdeeds.
Within the terrors of the miserable realms and their painful fruits, I, a fool, now seek your protection.
With the iron hook of great compassion, please grant me your guardianship as if I were your own beloved child;
protect me at all times. Thus concludes the verse of praise and prayer for the Great White Parasol Dhāraṇī.
